articles.title: The Biggest Surprises and Shocks from 2026 NFL Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The NFL is never short on surprises in the hours that lead up to final roster cuts. From the outside looking in, we're often left scratching our heads over moves that few expected to see on deadline day.
articles.body:
The NFL is never short on surprises in the hours that lead up to final roster cuts. From the outside looking in, we're often left scratching our heads over moves that few expected to see on deadline day.

This year, one of the biggest shockers was a playoff contender that turned a glaring weakness into a potentially bigger issue with a headline trade. Also, a few teams followed a roster-building blueprint that we haven't seen much in recent years.

Lastly, some clubs may regret cutting backups, both experienced and ascending players who could've provided quality depth.

Here are eight surprises and shocking moves from last Sunday's roster cuts deadline.

The Chicago Bears kicked off deadline day with arguably the most surprising move given their need for a pass-rusher.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Chicago traded Gervon Dexter Sr. to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick.

The Bears finished the 2025 season outside the top 20 in sacks and pressure rate. Dexter ranked second on the team in both categories behind edge-rusher Montez Sweat.

Per Fowler , the Bears have "big plans" for Jordan van den Berg. However, trading Dexter would leave Chicago relying more heavily on the rookie sixth-round pick along its defensive front.

It's also possible Bears general manager Ryan Poles had no intention of giving Dexter an extension during or after this season. The ascending defensive tackle is in the final year of his rookie deal.

Still, it's a surprise to see the Bears part ways with one of their most productive defensive linemen a year before they had to make a decision on his contract.

Broncos Waive Rookie Tight End Justin Joly

The Denver Broncos drafted two tight ends. Seventh-rounder Dallen Bentley made the team, and fifth-rounder Justin Joly missed the cut.

According to 9News' Mike Klis , Joly struggled through training camp, but he had a highlight moment on a long touchdown reception in the Broncos' preseason finale.

Andrew Mason of 104.3 The Fan believes Joly is the earliest draft pick in Broncos history who didn't make the 53-man roster.

Aside from Evan Engram, who's entering his age-32 campaign, the Broncos don't have a proven pass-catching tight end.

Joly caught 166 passes for 1,978 yards and 15 touchdowns in college. He brought a different skill set to Denver's tight end room, but his rough stretches at camp likely cost him a spot within a crowded position group.

The Washington Commanders are concerningly thin in the secondary with only three cornerbacks on the active roster.

Washington placed Trey Amos on injured reserve with a designation to return; he will miss at least four games. The club cut Fabian Moreau, Antonio Hamilton Sr., Darius Rush, Car'lin Vigers and Fred Davis II, which leaves Mike Sainristil and free-agent acquisitions Amik Robertson and Rasul Douglas at the position.

Washington will likely make moves to fill out its cornerback room, but the front office has just under two weeks to address the position before the team's season opener.

If the Commanders aren't active on waiver claims or the trade market for cornerbacks, they will have to bargain-bin shop on the late-offseason free-agent market.

Cowboys Waive Backup RBs Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah

Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah competed with Malik Davis for the No. 2 running back position. The young ball-carriers lost the battle and their roster spots.

The Athletic's Dane Brugler noted that Blue had "character concerns" in his pre-draft evaluation coming out of Texas. The Cowboys waived the 2025 fifth-round pick after one season.

Dallas selected Mafah in the seventh round of the same draft. He recorded two receptions for 11 yards in addition to five rush attempts for 18 yards and a touchdown last season.

According to ESPN's Todd Archer , Dallas also waived Israel Abanikanda.

The Cowboys will likely add multiple running backs to their practice squad. Still, they need Javonte Williams to stay healthy. Davis has been solid for fill-in duty, but he's logged just 90 carries for 411 yards and three touchdowns in four seasons.

Eagles, Falcons, Steelers and Vikings Keep 4 Quarterbacks

Four teams kept a quartet of quarterbacks.

The Atlanta Falcons' situation makes sense because Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. have extensive injury histories. It's possible they could start three or four different signal-callers this year. Journeyman Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand could see the field.

You can make a case as to why the Pittsburgh Steelers should keep four quarterbacks. They know 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers will retire after the 2026 season, and Mason Rudolph will be a free agent next year.

Rudolph is veteran insurance for Rodgers this year while the team develops rookie third-rounder Drew Allar and Will Howard, who sat out his rookie year because of a fractured pinkie on his throwing hand. In 2027, Allar and Howard can battle for the starting position.

The Vikings have an unsettled quarterback group. Kyler Murray is on a one-year deal, and he's played through just one full season over the last five years. Carson Wentz is also on a one-year deal. As a rookie last year, Max Brosmer appeared in seven games (made two starts). He threw four interceptions and zero touchdown passes.

J.J. McCarthy suffered an ankle injury in Week 2 of the preseason, which sidelined him for the team's last exhibition game. Despite being a 2024 first-round pick, his short-term future in Minnesota is uncertain after he lost the starting quarterback battle to Murray this offseason.

According to ESPN's Rich Cimini, as relayed by Philly Voice's Jimmy Kempski , the Eagles sought a second-round pick for Tanner McKee in March. Given that McKee has made only two career starts, that valuation may have limited Philadelphia's trade options.

Philadelphia acquired Andy Dalton from the Carolina Panthers and selected Cole Payton in the fifth round of this year's draft, which crowded the quarterback room.

With Jalen Hurts entering the season healthy, Philadelphia's additions of Dalton and Payton crowded a quarterback room that already included McKee. Still, general manager Howie Roseman has a strong track record of maximizing roster value.

It would be an even bigger surprise if any of these teams kept all four signal-callers for the entire 2026 campaign.

In June, the Atlanta Falcons traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for Wanya Morris and a 2027 seventh-round pick.

Atlanta didn't give up premium draft capital, but Morris could've provided depth behind Jake Matthews and free-agent acquisition Jawaan Taylor. Rookie seventh-rounder Ethan Onianwa and Michael Jerrell are the only other offensive tackles on the roster before Monday's waiver claims. Jerrell has played just 282 offensive snaps in two seasons.

With pocket passers Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. atop the depth chart, the Falcons could face a major concern in pass protection at tackle if Matthews or Taylor misses time.

Atlanta could be in search of an experienced veteran who's not subject to the waiver wire.

Trevin Wallace battled Claudin Cherelus for the inside linebacker spot alongside free-agent acquisition Devin Lloyd, who's coming off a Pro Bowl year with the Jacksonville Jaguars. In the end, Carolina went in another direction and signed eighth-year pro Bobby Okereke.

With 95 career starts, Okereke will likely take on a lead position despite his late arrival in Carolina. Yet it's a surprise that the team waived Wallace, who had a solid two-year run, logging 125 tackles, seven for loss, and four pass breakups in 25 games (20 starts).

Moreover, the Panthers selected Wallace in the third round of the 2024 draft, and he's only 23. At worst, the team could've retained him for depth, but Okereke's signing likely came at his expense.

The Pittsburgh Steelers signed Elandon Roberts, reuniting him with defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. They worked together with the Las Vegas Raiders last season, but the linebacker's familiarity with the system didn't work out in his favor.

Former Steeler James Harrison was surprised by this move and also questioned it on X:

"I hope we don't regret this cause I didn't see this coming in a million years.

"You telling me you brought this man in as a camp body??? Cause that's damn sure not what it sounded like was happening when he got here.

"We gon find out quick if this was a good decision or not in Week 1 vs Bijan though."

Roberts projected as a solid locker room addition in his second stint with the club, but the Steelers didn't have enough room for the 10-year pro who's been an above-average run defender.

Backup linebacker Cole Holcomb is in line to rotate with Patrick Queen and first-year full-time starter Payton Wilson.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Best Bargain Free Agents at Each Position After NFL 2026 Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The NFL's cutdown to 53 players passed on Sunday evening, but you can bet that teams aren't done tinkering with their rosters. With hundreds of experienced players flooding the free-agent market, teams will spend the next several days chasing upgrades.
articles.body:
The NFL's cutdown to 53 players passed on Sunday evening, but you can bet that teams aren't done tinkering with their rosters. With hundreds of experienced players flooding the free-agent market, teams will spend the next several days chasing upgrades.

Many teams will find ways to improve their rosters at a bargain rate, too.

Here, we'll examine the biggest potential bargains available at every position following the 53-man roster deadline—along with potential suitors—based on factors such as past production, experience, player upside, player health, and team needs.

A look at the biggest winners and losers from every team's roster cuts can be found here .

The free-agent market isn't loaded with starting-caliber quarterbacks, even after several signal-callers were dumped on Sunday. However, Jimmy Garoppolo is a former starter who can be a high-end backup and who has been available since the start of the offseason.

Garoppolo had considered retirement early in the offseason, but NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported in July that the former Super Bowl-starting QB is open to playing in 2026.

Josh Johnson, who was released by the Cincinnati Bengals, is another seasoned quarterback with the experience needed to be a high-end backup. The 40-year-old has been in the NFL since 2008, has played in 50 games with 11 starts, and has appeared in games for seven different franchises.

Johnson's familiarity with many different offensive systems should allow him to step right into a valuable depth role.

Yes, Will Levis quickly became a punchline with the Tennessee Titans, but it's not as if Tennessee has the best recent track record of developing quarterbacks. Teams may have interest in trying to develop the former second-round pick after remembering how Malik Willis flourished after getting out of Tennessee.

Potential Suitors: Jacksonville Jaguars, New York Jets

Jerome Ford's health remains a bit of an unknown. After he suffered a hamstring injury, the Washington Commanders waived him with an injury settlement, according to ESPN's John Keim .

However, Ford is a solid RB2 when healthy who showed he can be a viable spot-starter during his time with the Cleveland Browns. He topped 1,100 scrimmage yards in 2023, and he has averaged 4.3 yards per carry as a pro.

The Denver Broncos released Jaleel McLaughlin from their crowded RB room, and the speedy Youngstown State product should interest teams seeking a change-of-pace back.

Over the last three years with Denver, McLaughlin tallied 1,356 scrimmage yards while averaging an impressive 4.8 yards per carry. He's a bit undersized (5'7", 187 lbs) but possesses big-play ability and won't turn 26 until mid-September.

Jaydon Blue, who was released by the Dallas Cowboys, doesn't have much of an NFL resume. What he does have is a lot of untapped potential. While Blue appeared in only five games as a rookie, he recorded 1,098 scrimmage yards and 14 touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry at Texas in 2024.

Potential Suitors: Jacksonville Jaguars, Seattle Seahawks

The Las Vegas Raiders are in the early stages of a rebuild and opted to release 30-year-old wideout Noah Brown after a short stint with the team. However, Brown would be a strong option for a contender looking for proven depth at the position.

Brown appeared in only four games for the Commanders last season because of groin and rib injuries. However, he caught 35 passes for 453 yards and a touchdown in 2024. Since entering the NFL in 2017, he has appeared in 91 regular-season games and caught 151 passes for 2,083 yards.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who was released by the Cowboys, is another seasoned veteran who should appeal to contenders seeking depth. He appeared in five games each with the San Francisco 49ers and Pittsburgh Steelers last season, and he has appeared in 116 regular-season games over his eight-year career.

Valdes-Scantling also won a pair of Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs and has recorded 432 receiving yards and four touchdowns in the postseason.

Cedric Tillman is a younger and far less proven receiver who could appeal to rebuilding teams. He was released by the Cleveland Browns after recording just 833 yards in three seasons.

Of course, Tillman's growth was hampered by some bad Browns offenses, and the 6'3", 215-pound pass-catcher has flashed some intriguing upside. He had 330 yards and three touchdowns in a five-game stretch before suffering a season-ending concussion in 2024.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Miami Dolphins

Tight end Donald Parham was on Denver's practice squad in 2024 and missed all of last season with an Achilles injury, but he appears ready to contribute in 2026.

Washington hosted him for a tryout before the start of training camp, according to Ian Saunders of SteelersNow.com (h/t RotoWire ).

If Parham is indeed back near pre-injury form, he should be an intriguing option for teams seeking a pass-catcher at the position. In 2023, he appeared in 14 games for the Chargers and caught 27 passes for 285 yards and four touchdowns.

Pharaoh Brown has never put up gaudy receiving numbers in the NFL, but he's carved out an eight-year career as an in-line blocking tight end. He appeared in only seven games with the Arizona Cardinals last season but has appeared in 94 games with 56 starts overall.

Brown was released by the Indianapolis Colts.

Justin Joly has no regular-season NFL experience, as he was just drafted by the Broncos in April. However, the fifth-round pick out of North Carolina State did impress during Denver's preseason finale with an 88-yard touchdown catch-and-run.

The Broncos have a loaded roster, but not every team does. Someone will find room to develop Joly.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Miami Dolphins

Former Detroit Lions starting left tackle Taylor Decker remains available since being granted his release early in the offseason. He should still be the top option for any team that needs a starter or backup at the left tackle position.

Decker has started all 140 regular-season games in which he has appeared, has logged five playoff starts, and made the Pro Bowl in 2024. Cam Robinson hasn't played as well recently, but the available left tackle made 13 starts last season and has 114 for his career.

Kevin Zeitler has been available all offseason and should interest teams unhappy with their guard rotation heading into Week 1.

Zeitler has made a whopping 213 NFL starts, including 16 in each of the past two seasons. He was surrounded by an underwhelming Titans line in 2025 and still managed to finish ranked 13th overall among guards by Pro Football Focus .

Cody Ford was released by the Bengals after spending the last three seasons as one of their primary backups. While Ford has never established himself as a high-end starter, he has appeared in 99 games and logged snaps at left guard, right guard, and offensive tackle.

Ford is a backup, but his positional versatility should interest several teams.

Former New York Giants first-round pick Evan Neal will only interest teams willing to take on a reclamation project. The seventh overall pick in the 2022 draft failed to pan out at tackle or guard for the Giants and spent last season on injured reserve. However, he's still only 25 years old.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Washington Commanders

DaQuan Jones may be 34 years old, but he remains a starting-caliber defensive tackle. He was limited to 12 games in Buffalo last season by calf issues, but he started all 12 of those contests and tallied 22 tackles with three sacks and eight quarterback hits.

Jones met with the Patriots in mid-August, according to Mike Reiss of ESPN, but he remains a potential bargain for any team in need of an immediate contributor along the defensive line.

Mazi Smith may not make an impact right away, but he's an intriguing developmental candidate who could pay long-term dividends. Smith, whom the New York Jets recently released, was a first-round pick of the Cowboys in 2023 and is still only 25 years old.

Smith hasn't come close to playing up to his draft status, but he possesses an attractive combination of youth, size (6'3", 337 lbs), and upside.

The Colts released defensive tackle Colby Wooden just a few months after acquiring him in a March trade with the Green Bay Packers. While Wooden didn't pan out in Indy, he started 16 games for Green Bay last season and recorded 50 tackles.

Emmanuel Ogbah has been a quality rotational defensive end for most of his 10-year career and even has a pair of nine-sack seasons on his resume. He has appeared in 136 total games with 90 starts.

Ogbah appeared in 13 games for the Jacksonville Jaguars last season and was just released by the Kansas City Chiefs.

Defensive lineman Carlos Watkins was released by the Titans. While he only appeared in three games for Tennessee last season, the 32-year-old appeared in 15 games for the Cowboys the previous season and has appeared in 90 games across nine seasons.

Potential Suitors: Las Vegas Raiders, New York Giants

Kyle Van Noy has filled a few different defensive roles during his time in the NFL, but he has most recently served as a rotational edge-rusher for the Baltimore Ravens. He recorded just two sacks in 2025 but also logged 17 QB pressures in a rotational role and has been more prolific in the recent past.

In three seasons with Baltimore, Van Noy recorded 23.5 sacks and 54 quarterback pressures.

BJ Ojulari was hoping to establish himself as a dependable defensive force when a 2024 knee injury derailed that plan. Ojulari tore multiple ligaments in his left knee during Cardinals training camp and didn't return to the field until late in 2025.

The 2023 second-round pick recorded four sacks and five tackles for loss and could reward teams willing to bet on his upside. Though Arizona opted to release him, Ojulari was cleared to play in 2026 and is still only 24 years old.

Sam Williams is another former second-round pick who suffered a significant knee injury in 2024. The Cowboys released the 2022 Mississippi product after completely rebuilding their pass-rushing rotation this offseason. However, Williams flashed early in his career with 8.5 sacks in his first two seasons.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers

Linebacker Bobby Wagner is probably only interested in playing for a contender at this point in his career. However, the future Hall of Famer should be willing to join a playoff hopeful on a relatively budget-friendly deal.

Wagner played on a one-year, $9 million contract with Washington last season. While that's obviously not a league-minimum price, the Commanders got a strong return on investment. Wagner finished the 2025 season with 162 tackles, 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, and two interceptions.

Tyrel Dodson doesn't carry the lengthy resume that Wagner does, but the 28-year-old possesses long-term starting potential.

Dodson was released by the Miami Dolphins but started 16 games for them in 2025 and recorded 129 tackles, five sacks, 10 tackles for loss, and three passes defended. He has started 43 games as a pro and is highly unlikely to remain available for long.

Elandon Roberts was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after making 16 starts for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025. The 32-year-old has 30 starts over the past two seasons and 121 for his career.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Denver Broncos

Early in the offseason, the Colts and cornerback Kenny Moore II agreed to try to work out a trade. After one failed to materialize, Moore was released instead. He's been available since May, a fact that has even surprised former NFL star cornerback Stephon Gilmore.

Moore is a terrific target for teams seeking production and positional versatility in the secondary. He recently turned 31 and made just seven starts in 2025, but he also has 111 starts on his resume and allowed an opposing passer rating of just 87.8 in coverage last season.

Adoree' Jackson is another seasoned vet whose presence on the open market is a bit surprising. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Jackson has drawn interest from "a few teams" over the summer.

Jackson made 10 starts for the Eagles last season and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 80.2 in coverage. The 30-year-old has appeared in 111 regular-season games with 92 starts.

Travon Diggs was once one of the biggest takeaway threats in the NFL, but he hasn't quite been the same since his 2023 knee injury. He's still only 27, though, and showed during the preseason that he can still make a play on the ball.

The Seattle Seahawks released Diggs, but GM John Schneider has said that he plans to add Diggs to the practice squad (h/t Gregg Bell of the Tacoma News Tribune). Here's where we remind fans that players can be signed off the practice squad to another team's active roster.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers

Safety Taylor Rapp signed with the Broncos in August and may not remain available for long. Head coach Sean Payton told reporters that Rapp was stepping away to attend to a personal matter and is a strong candidate to re-sign in Denver (h/t Zac Stevens of DNVR).

If the Broncos aren't quick to bring back Rapp, he would be a terrific addition to any defense lacking safety depth. He has made 72 starts while allowing an opposing passer rating of 91.0 in his career, and he has experience at both strong and free safety.

Geno Stone has also logged snaps at strong and free safety. The former Ravens standout spent the past two seasons in Cincinnati, starting all 34 regular-season games for the Bengals.

Stone, who is still only 27 years old, tallied a career-high 104 tackles to go with two sacks and two interceptions last season. Nevertheless, the Buffalo Bills released him during roster cuts.

The Dolphins released Lonnie Johnson Jr., who has largely been a rotational safety and special-teamer during his seven-year career. Johnson has appeared in 90 games, though, and has seen time at both safety and cornerback.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions

articles.title: Cheat Sheet to Every NFL Team's Backup QBs for 2026 Season After Roster Cuts
articles.summary: One thing the NFL has taught us over the years is that, while backup quarterbacks are often underappreciated, they fill one of the most important roles in football.
articles.body:
One thing the NFL has taught us over the years is that, while backup quarterbacks are often underappreciated, they fill one of the most important roles in football.

Ideally, a team with an established starter won't need to rely on its understudy. However, injuries can't be entirely avoided, and having a good spot-starter can mean the difference between a successful season and a disaster.

Just last season, we saw the Houston Texans and San Francisco 49ers survive multi-game stretches with their backup QBs and reach the playoffs. Conversely, the Indianapolis Colts failed to adequately replace Daniel Jones and watched an 8-2 start devolve into an 8-9 finish.

Not every team enters 2026 with a high-level starter, of course, and some backups will find their way onto the field in the coming weeks based on performance instead of injury. With roster cuts complete, however, now is the perfect time to examine every team's Plan B at QB.

The Arizona Cardinals released Kyler Murray early in the offseason and have decided to make former backup Jacoby Brissett their Week 1 starter. Waiting in the wings behind Brissett, however, will be rookie third-round pick Carson Beck .

Beck looked impressive in the preseason opener and may have challenged for the starting job if the rib injury he suffered in the Hall of Fame Game hadn't sidelined him for the rest of the preseason. It feels almost inevitable that he'll make starts for Arizona in 2026.

If and when Brissett stumbles or the Cardinals fall firmly out of playoff contention, the Cardinals are going to want to get a look at what they have in their rookie.

However, journeyman quarterback Gardner Minshew is likely to be Brissett's primary backup early in the season. He has 47 starts on his resume and is well-equipped to enter a game at a moment's notice.

The Atlanta Falcons were expected to hold a quarterback competition between 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. and free-agent addition Tua Tagovailoa. However, Penix missed much of camp and the preseason while recovering from a torn ACL, so there hasn't been much actual competition.

Tagovailoa may win the Week 1 job by default, though head coach Kevin Stefanski is delaying his decision.

"Whenever they tell me I have to, when that depth chart has to be put out," Stefanski said of his timeline for naming a starter, per NFL.com's Nick Shook .

Teams are required to produce an official depth chart ahead of Week 1, so that's probably when we'll know who will get the first crack at QB1. Barring a surprise, it'll be either Tagovailoa or Penix, with the one who doesn't start slotting in as QB2.

The Baltimore Ravens have one of the NFL's best backup QB plans.

Lamar Jackson is an elite dual-threat starter who can play at an MVP level when at his best. Backup Tyler Huntley is a dual-threat signal-caller who can start multiple games and deliver multiple wins if needed.

Huntley went 2-2 for the Ravens in 2022 and was named to the Pro Bowl as an alternate for his efforts.

Obviously, Huntley isn't the same caliber of quarterback as Jackson. However, his similar playing style and experience with Baltimore's personnel mean that if he has to enter the lineup for any stretch, the Ravens won't need to make significant adjustments.

Breaking down winners and losers from NFL cut day

Josh Allen was the league MVP just two years ago, and if he misses any significant time, the Buffalo Bills will be in trouble. However, the Bills do have an experienced backup in Kyle Allen.

Kyle Allen was Josh Allen's understudy in 2023 before spending the last two seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Detroit Lions. The 30-year-old hasn't started a game since 2022, but he has 19 starts on his resume and a respectable (for a backup) 7-12 record.

The Bills may not be sunk if they need Kyle Allen to play a few series or even an entire game. However, he isn't likely to deliver multiple wins if Josh Allen is forced to miss an extended stretch.

The Carolina Panthers had one of the league's better backup quarterbacks in Andy Dalton. However, they traded the three-time Pro Bowler to the Philadelphia Eagles in March.

With Dalton gone, the Panthers turned to free agent and 2022 first-round pick Kenny Pickett.

While Pickett never established himself as an above-average starter, he does hold a 16-11 record. He also possesses a skill set—one centered around accuracy, anticipation, and pocket awareness—that isn't overly dissimilar to that of starter Bryce Young.

Pickett won't threaten Young as Carolina's quarterback of the future, but he could help the Panthers pick up a couple of wins if Young is sidelined.

The Chicago Bears have their franchise quarterback in 2025 breakout star Caleb Williams. They also have a backup they love in Tyson Bagent. The 2023 undrafted free agent out of Shepherd went 2-2 as a starter the year before Williams was drafted and has a skill set well-suited for Williams' understudy.

Bagent isn't a true dual-threat, but he can buy time in the pocket and scramble, as evidenced by the 109 rushing yards and two rushing scores he produced in his five 2023 appearances.

The Bears should feel good about their ability to pick up a win or two if they need to rely on Bagent as a spot-starter—and they obviously do. Chicago signed Bagent to a two-year, $10 million extension last offseason.

Cincinnati Bengals starter Joe Burrow had another injury-hampered season in 2025, and the Bengals traded for aging veteran Joe Flacco to help navigate it. While the former Super Bowl MVP only went 1-5 as Cincinnati's starter last season, that had more to do with an atrocious Bengals defense than Flacco's ability.

Flacco quickly meshed with top targets Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and finished his six-game stint with 13 touchdown passes and a 91.0 QB rating.

Even at 41, Flacco has the arm talent needed to fit right into Zac Taylor's offense. He isn't Burrow, of course, but the Bengals know that they can still field a potent offense with Flacco at the helm.

And now that Cincinnati has finally put some effort into reloading its defense, it can probably expect to play winning football if Flacco has to replace Burrow for another stretch.

The Cleveland Browns held an offseason quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. While neither competitor truly seemed to take a firm hold on the QB1 job, new head coach Todd Monken named Watson as the Week 1 starter after Cleveland's second preseason game.

However, this doesn't mean Sanders won't make starts in 2026. The simple reality is that if the Browns struggle early, pivoting to a young quarterback will be easier to justify than pivoting to a veteran who has largely disappointed with the franchise.

This also doesn't mean Sanders won't ultimately outperform Watson when he gets his opportunity. Watson's uneven play for the Browns, however, could give Cleveland reason to consider a change if it struggles early.

Neither Watson nor Sanders is going to make Cleveland a title contender or prevent the franchise from battling for 2027 draft positioning late in the season. And given the Browns' recent habit of starting multiple QBs, fans can probably expect to see some of Dillon Gabriel and/or Taylen Green before this transition year is over.

Technically, the Dallas Cowboys may not have a clear-cut backup behind Dak Prescott. Joe Milton III filled that role in 2025 but battled Sam Howell for the QB2 job during the summer with no clear winner.

"That's one that we may just split the difference and have two backup quarterbacks here," team owner Jerry Jones said, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

Dallas kept Milton and Howell on the initial 53-man roster, and both made the highlight reel during the preseason. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer may feel comfortable turning to either signal-caller if Prescott is forced to miss time.

However, Milton is the incumbent and will likely get the first nod if a backup is needed.

Denver Broncos starter Bo Nix has fully recovered from offseason ankle surgery and, after seeing limited preseason action, should be a full-go for Week 1. If Nix suffers another injury, though, the Broncos will be able to turn to a backup with playoff experience.

Jarrett Stidham took the reins for last year's AFC Championship game after Nix suffered a fractured ankle late in the divisional round victory. He didn't play well enough to put Denver in the Super Bowl, but he kept the team competitive during its 10-7 loss to the New England Patriots in wintry conditions.

Stidham can also keep the Broncos afloat if he's forced to start a game or two during the 2026 season. He obviously lacks Nix's physical ability, but the Auburn product has five total starts on his resume and has spent the last three years in Sean Payton's offense.

In March, the Detroit Lions brought back Teddy Bridgewater for another run as Jared Goff's backup. However, he decided to retire in August, forcing the Lions to turn to Joshua Dobbs.

The good news is that, even if Dobbs wasn't Detroit's first choice for a backup, he's a good one. The 2017 fourth-round pick out of Tennessee has bounced around the league in a variety of roles but has also made 15 starts and performed well when given a strong supporting cast—he went 2-2 as the Minnesota Vikings' starter in 2023.

Dobbs also spent part of 2023 with the Cardinals, playing under offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, who now holds the same title in Detroit. He has looked extremely comfortable in Petzing's offense during the preseason and should be well-prepared for spot duty in the off chance the Lions call on him.

Goff has started all 17 games in each of the past four seasons.

Whenever Jordan Love was sidelined over the past two years, the Green Bay Packers were able to count on backup Malik Willis.

After going 2-1 with a 134.6 quarterback rating, though, Willis landed a three-year, $67.5 million contract from the Miami Dolphins in free agency.

With Willis gone, the Packers turned to veteran Tyrod Taylor as Love's backup. Taylor does not have the same physical upside as Love or Willis, but his similar playing style should allow Green Bay to make a seamless schematic transition if Love misses a game or two in 2026.

Taylor also has the experience needed to be a locker-room leader and, possibly, even a mentor to Love. The 37-year-old has appeared in 100 games with 62 starts and has posted an 87.7 passer rating. While Taylor hasn't been a regular starter since 2017, he holds a 29-31-1 record and remains one of the league's top backups.

The Houston Texans have yet to commit to starting quarterback C.J. Stroud with a lucrative second contract. However, they did commit to backup Davis Mills with a one-year, $7 million extension in 2025.

Mills has proven himself to be a capable spot-starter for the Texans, even if he didn't deliver many wins early in his career. Thrust into a starting role as a rookie, the 2021 third-round pick went just 5-19-1 in his first two seasons with Houston.

Of course, the Texans were a struggling team then. As a three-game starter this past season, Mills went undefeated while throwing for 915 yards with five touchdowns and an interception.

Mills isn't going to threaten Stroud's job security, but he can keep the Texans on track for a deep playoff run if he needs to start a handful of regular-season games or even a postseason contest.

To be fair, this is another instance where a team may have two backups instead of one defined understudy. The Indianapolis Colts kept Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard on their initial 53-man roster, but they're both listed in the second-team slot on the early unofficial depth chart .

Leonard saw playing time after Daniel Jones' season-ending Achilles injury, but it's worth noting that Richardson was on injured reserve with an orbital fracture. Richardson also out-played Leonard during the preseason, though that hasn't led to any official announcement of him earning the backup job.

Richardson's combination of arm strength and scrambling ability might make him the best option to enter a game for a series or two, as he could keep a defense off-balance temporarily. However, the Colts are unlikely to win a stretch of games with either quarterback if Jones goes down—Indy went 0-4 without him last season.

Ideally, though, it's an issue that will never emerge. Jones has recovered and is ready to start in Week 1.

The Jacksonville Jaguars appear to be betting heavily on Trevor Lawrence's ability to stay healthy in 2026.

Jacksonville had a seasoned backup in Nick Mullens last season, but the Jaguars recently traded for Miami Dolphins backup Quinn Ewers. Mullens was subsequently released.

Ewers was a 2025 seventh-round pick out of Texas and went 1-2 with an 85.5 QB rating in three starts for the Dolphins last season. He may possess more long-term upside than Mullens. However, his lack of experience could lead to a lot of QB questions if Lawrence misses a significant stretch this season.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is making his way back from a torn ACL, but he was cleared in time for training camp and will be behind center in Week 1.

If Mahomes is forced to miss time, though, fans can expect to see Justin Fields filling in.

Rookie seventh-round pick Garrett Nussmeier impressed during the preseason, and there's a good chance that he'll become Mahomes' understudy for the long term. However, Fields offers a blend of experience and athletic ability that makes him an intriguing potential spot-starter.

Fields, a first-round pick of the Bears back in 2021, has appeared in 59 games with 53 starts. He could keep the Chiefs offense rolling for a few series or even a full game, and his elite scrambling ability may give Andy Reid some change-of-pace options.

Of course, Fields has never been particularly consistent as a passer. If Mahomes were to miss an extended stretch, Kansas City might consider making the pivot to Nussmeier.

The Las Vegas Raiders added veteran Kirk Cousins before they used the No. 1 overall pick on Indiana product and reigning Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza . The plan all along has been to let Mendoza sit and learn from Cousins, and that plan still appears to be in effect.

According to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz , the Raiders are indeed expected to name Cousins their starting quarterback.

This should push Mendoza into the QB2 role. He is the future, and Las Vegas will want every chance it can get to work on his development in practices. If the Raiders need a QB replacement in-game during the regular season, however, they may first turn to the more experienced Aidan O'Connell.

O'Connell has made 17 starts in his three seasons with Las Vegas.

In Week 1, the Los Angeles Chargers' quarterback room will probably look a lot like it did in 2025. Justin Herbert is the unquestioned starter, and last year's backup, Trey Lance, remains in the fold behind him.

2025 undrafted free agent DJ Uiagalelei, who spent last season on the practice squad, should again be the emergency option. Lance isn't a particularly experienced NFL quarterback, having made just six starts since being drafted third overall in 2021. However, he has elite athletic potential and could give the Chargers a fighting chance if forced into the lineup.

The Chargers won't be contenders if they have to play an extended stretch without Herbert, but, fortunately for them, Herbert has been a durable starter and more likely than not to play through injury.

The Los Angeles Rams just used the 13th overall pick on Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson despite having the reigning MVP in Matthew Stafford. Naturally, this means Simpson will be Stafford's primary understudy in 2026, right? Actually, he probably won't.

Simpson may be the long-term heir to Stafford in L.A., but he's still a bit of a project. Stetson Bennett IV, a 2023 fourth-round pick, appears more prepared to play now if needed.

Bennett stepped away from the Rams during his rookie season in 2023, later saying the absence related to his mental health. He has since spent two years learning Sean McVay's offense. Bennett performed well during the preseason and did not play in L.A.'s preseason finale as the Rams evaluated rookie Ty Simpson in the backup-quarterback competition.

McVay runs a QB-friendly offense and Los Angeles boasts a stacked roster, so the Rams might be able to win a game or two if Stafford misses time. However, neither Bennett nor Simpson has NFL starting experience, so the Rams can't expect a seamless transition if the MVP goes down.

To be fair, the Dolphins don't know exactly what they have in new starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Liberty product showed a tremendous amount of ability as a spot-starter in Green Bay, but he has just six starts on his resume.

Miami largely won't know what to expect if Willis can't stay healthy in 2026, either, though new head coach Jeff Hafley has brought in another familiar face.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Dolphins have acquired Kyle McCord from the Packers in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.

McCord never appeared in a regular-season game for Green Bay. However, he did impress in the Packers' preseason finale, throwing for 226 yards and four touchdowns. He also has some experience with Hafley, who came to Miami after serving as the Packers' defensive coordinator.

The Minnesota Vikings' quarterback competition between free-agent addition Kyler Murray and 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy was a short one.

The Vikings named Murray the starter relatively early in training camp, which left McCarthy vying for the backup role.

It would appear that Minnesota would prefer the veteran presence of Carson Wentz filling the QB2 job.

"McCarthy's comfort (or lack thereof) with being QB3 could dictate his future in Minnesota," Alec Lewis of The Athletic wrote after the Vikings' preseason finale, in which McCarthy did not play.

McCarthy did make the initial 53-man roster, but going with Wentz is the sensible move if the Vikings view themselves as contenders. He's a former Pro Bowler with 99 starts and an 89.1 quarterback rating. He isn't going to threaten Murray's status as QB1, and he can provide a steady hand if Murray misses time.

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was the NFL MVP runner-up last season, and the Patriots obviously hope that he can stay healthy for the entire season. If Maye does have to miss a bit of time, however, New England should be able to stay competitive by turning to Tommy DeVito.

DeVito entered the NFL as a 2023 undrafted free agent out of Illinois, but he became a rookie sensation with the New York Giants when pressed into action due to injuries. He was claimed off waivers by New England last offseason and was moved up the depth chart in the spring.

The Patriots signed DeVito to a two-year, $4.4 million deal and released former backup Joshua Dobbs.

While DeVito has gone just 3-5 as an NFL starter, he has played mostly well (88.4 QB rating) and has flashed enough dual-threat ability to be an appropriate backup for Maye. Seventh-round rookie Behren Morton also made the initial roster.

Tyler Shough cemented himself as the New Orleans Saints' starter late in his rookie season. Entering Year 2, there are no questions about his job security. However, the Saints still have some questions about who their primary backup will be.

Spencer Rattler opened last season as the starter and has a full season in head coach Kellen Moore's offense. However, free-agent addition Zac Wilson is a former first-round pick who has 33 starts on his resume. It appears that New Orleans will carry both into Week 1.

"Both these guys are capable of playing and being really successful quarterbacks," Moore said, per Schuyler Dixon of the Associated Press. "Spencer and Zac are going to provide excellent depth for us."

Rattler should be Shough's chief understudy because of his experience in New Orleans. However, he has a 1-13 record as the Saints' starter, and Wilson (12-21) has never been a dependable QB1.

In other words, New Orleans had better hope that Shough can stay on the field.

The New York Giants' hope is that second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart will avoid the blue medical tent in 2026 and improve upon his promising rookie season. If the Mississippi product does miss time, however, New York will have a very experienced quarterback to take the reins.

Jameis Winston, who joined New York on a two-year, $8 million deal last offseason, was the first overall pick in the 2015 draft. He has 89 starts on his resume and has thrown for 24,792 yards and 156 touchdowns.

Winston can keep New York's offense humming and can deliver a win or two if Dart is forced to miss multiple games. The problem is that he remains a bit reckless with the football and could just as easily cost the Giants games with turnovers.

Back in 2019, Winston reached 30 touchdown passes and 30 interceptions in the same season.

The Giants are unlikely to see a major drop-off if Winston has to start for a stretch in 2026, but they aren't going to see him spark a deep playoff run either.

The New York Jets are banking on Geno Smith, a quarterback they originally drafted back in 2013 and who they re-acquired this offseason in a trade. While Smith didn't perform well in Las Vegas last season, he's a two-time Pro Bowler who has shown he can be a high-end game manager.

Smith can provide some reliability at quarterback, but if he misses time, the QB position in New York will become far more volatile. The Jets released veteran Bailey Zappe, leaving rookie fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik as New York's primary insurance policy—at least for now.

While Klubnik had a few flashes in the preseason, he didn't wow, and he obviously has no NFL starting experience. The Jets may eventually turn to Klubnik to see what the rookie can do, but no one should be surprised if they look to add a veteran backup in the coming days.

After all, the Jets did consider adding Russell Wilson as Smith's backup early in the offseason.

The Philadelphia Eagles' backup situation is a bit murky, as there is no clear-cut backup to starter Jalen Hurts. Presumably, it'll be either Tanner McKee or Andy Dalton, and Philly may try to flip one of the two in a trade before Week 1.

McKee was the Eagles' backup in 2025, but he's entering the final year of his rookie contract and drew trade interest early in the offseason, according to Cayden Steele of NJ.com. Dalton was acquired in a trade in March.

Philly kept both backups on the initial roster, along with fifth-round rookie Cole Payton .

The Eagles may still be sorting out who will be QB2 and/or seeing if one of their backups has trade value. However, none of the quarterbacks sitting behind Hurts are likely to string together more than a couple of wins if the starter goes down.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have Aaron Rodgers as their starter for one more season. It appears that they'll have Mason Rudolph, second-year man Will Howard, and rookie third-rounder Drew Allar waiting in the wings behind him.

"I've been saying it for quite some time, and they've showed it on the field," head coach Mike McCarthy said, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor . "We got two veterans that we can win with, and we got two young guys that we're excited about the future."

If the Steelers' season goes awry, they may want to get a look at one or both of their young signal-callers. However, Rudolph is the logical gameday backup behind Rodgers because of his experience.

Rudolph has shown that he can be a capable placeholder or spot-starter. He has 20 total starts on his resume and has even started a playoff game for Pittsburgh.

Do the San Francisco 49ers have the best backup QB in the league? That's debatable, but they have the perfect backup for Kyle Shanahan's system and a signal-caller who would upgrade a few QB rooms around the NFL—and San Francisco knows it.

According to The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt , the 49ers want a second-round pick for Jones.

Jones started eight games last season while Brock Purdy was out with a toe injury and went 5-3 with a 97.4 QB rating. He isn't quite as good as San Francisco's starter, who went 7-2 with a 100.5 QB rating last season. However, the 49ers won't fall out of playoff contention if Purdy has another extended absence.

The Seattle Seahawks found a quarterback they can win with when they signed Sam Darnold in 2025 free agency. The 2018 Jets first-round pick had his second straight Pro Bowl campaign last season while helping Seattle win Super Bowl LX.

While the Seahawks certainly hope they don't have to try winning without Darnold in 2026, they have an experienced understudy in Drew Lock. The 2019 second-round pick was with Seattle in 2023 and returned last season to provide backup duties.

While Lock has never established himself as a quality starter, he has 28 starts on his resume and an 81.0 quarterback rating as a Seahawk. Seattle also has 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe, who remains a project but who could complement Lock as a package player.

Seattle isn't likely to return to the Super Bowl if Darnold goes down for an extended period, but it is positioned to navigate a handful of absences.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven't needed to rely on a backup quarterback since Baker Mayfield took over in 2023. If Mayfield does miss time in 2026, though, Tampa will turn to a promising undrafted free agent.

On Sunday, the Bucs named rookie Jalon Daniels as the backup.

"He's shown a lot," head coach Todd Bowles said, per ESPN .

Daniels did indeed flash during the preseason, and the Kansas product had his fair share of bright moments in college, too. He appeared in 49 games over six seasons and finished his 2025 campaign with 2,531 passing yards, 404 rushing yards, and 26 combined rushing and passing touchdowns.

Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward didn't have overly impressive numbers as a rookie in 2025, but he isn't in danger of being benched in Year 2. He flashed some very intriguing upside while also playing with one of the league's worst supporting casts. The Titans and new head coach Robert Saleh will want to see what Ward can accomplish with a better group.

If Ward is forced to come off the field this season, though, Tennessee has a strong backup plan. It signed Mitchell Trubisky to a two-year, $10.5 million deal in the offseason in order to provide insurance and some mentorship to the offense.

Trubisky has 57 starts on his resume, a 31-26 record, and an 86.9 career quarterback rating. He also has experience with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll after playing under him as Buffalo's backup in 2021.

Ward has a much higher ceiling than Trubisky at this point in their respective careers. However, Tennessee probably wouldn't experience much of a drop-off if forced to turn to Trubisky as a spot-starter this season.

Two years ago, the Washington Commanders reached the NFC title game with then-rookie Jayden Daniels at quarterback. Unfortunately, injuries limited Daniels to seven starts in 2025, and Washington finished with a 5-12 record.

Backup Marcus Mariota went just 2-6 in his eight starts last season before he was sidelined by injuries of his own. However, all of Washington's quarterbacks were hampered by a bad defense and other injuries to the offensive supporting cast.

While Mariota has dealt with a sprained MCL in the preseason, head coach Dan Quinn has been optimistic about his ability to be available in Week 1, according to ESPN's John Keim .

Mariota, who has 82 starts on his resume, is actually one of the league's best backups. He holds an 89.7 career QB rating and possesses a dual-threat skill set that meshes with any game plan Washington has crafted for Daniels. If the Commanders' roster is truly playoff-caliber this season, they can win a few games with Mariota if necessary.

articles.title: New 'Game Day Murders' Episode Covers Life and Death of NFL Star Sean Taylor on HBO Max
articles.summary: The 2007 death of former star NFL safety Sean Taylor will be covered during Monday's episode of Game Day Murders from Investigation Discovery.
articles.body:
The 2007 death of former star NFL safety Sean Taylor will be covered during Monday's episode of Game Day Murders from Investigation Discovery.

It will be the latest edition of the six-episode Game Day Murders series, which was executive produced by NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal. Episodes air at 10 p.m. ET on ID and are available for streaming on HBO Max.

"I've been a true-crime guy my whole life, so working with ID on GAME DAY MURDERS was a natural fit," O'Neal said in a press release. "Sports create obsession—I've seen it firsthand. But when that obsession breaks the wrong way, it's something else entirely. People aren't ready for this show."

Monday's episode, which is titled Blindsided by Tragedy , will feature commentary from Taylor's former Washington teammate Santana Moss and explore the safety's death that occurred when he was shot during a home invasion.

Taylor was just 24 years old when he died.

In 2014, Curt Anderson of the Associated Press reported Eric Rivera, who was the man prosecutors said fired the shot during the burglary that killed Taylor, was sentenced to more than 57 years in state prison.

Taylor first became a household name as a star safety for the Miami Hurricanes. He was the 2003 Big East Defensive Player of the Year and a consensus All-American who helped lead the program to back-to-back double-digit win seasons.

Washington selected him with the No. 5 pick of the 2004 NFL draft, and he quickly established himself as one of the best safeties in the league. He was known for his physical style of play that helped him patrol the middle of the field, but he was also a ballhawk with 12 interceptions in 55 games.

Taylor was a back-to-back Pro Bowler during his final two seasons in 2006 and 2007.

Washington retired his No. 21 during the 2021 campaign and also inducted him into the franchise's Ring of Fame.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes on their way to becoming billionaires? The fortune behind their lavish lifestyle
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has already conquered the NFL, but his ambitions extend far beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has turned h.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has already conquered the NFL, but his ambitions extend far beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has turned his enormous playing income and superstar profile into a growing portfolio of business and sports investments. With ownership stakes, endorsement deals, real estate and brand partnerships adding to his wealth, Mahomes is building an empire that could eventually push him into billionaire territory.Patrick Mahomes is building a business empire beyond his NFL salaryMahomes' biggest financial asset remains his Chiefs contract. He signed a 10-year, $450 million deal in 2020, a landmark agreement at the time. Although several quarterbacks now command higher annual salaries, Mahomes has something many of his rivals cannot match: exceptional earning power away from the field.Forbes estimated his off-field earnings at $25 million in 2024, making him the NFL's most marketable athlete by a considerable margin. His popularity also translates into merchandise sales, with his No. 15 jersey ranking among the league's biggest sellers.His commercial portfolio is equally broad. Mahomes has worked with Adidas on a signature collection and has appeared in campaigns for major names including State Farm, Subway, T-Mobile, Oakley and Head & Shoulders. He has also been associated with Prime, the beverage company founded by Logan Paul and KSI.But endorsements are only one part of the bigger picture.The quarterback has steadily moved into ownership. He holds an interest in the Kansas City Royals and has invested in Sporting Kansas City. His sports portfolio has also extended into Formula One through an investment in Alpine, alongside a group that has included fellow stars from different sporting worlds.That move fits Mahomes' competitive personality. He previously explained why the opportunity appealed to him:“I think everybody can see the appeal.“I’ve been able to get to a couple races now, seeing the environment, and then obviously watching the Drive to Survive on Netflix you see how competitive it is.“Any time you get an opportunity to get in on that, I mean I’m as competitive as anyone can get, so hopefully it can open up to some great opportunities and we are able to go to some of those races and have a little stake in the game.”Patrick Mahomes' investments stretch into wellness and real estateMahomes has also been putting money into businesses outside traditional sports. His investment interests have included Whoop, the wearable technology company focused on fitness and performance data, and Hyperice, where he became both an ambassador and equity holder.Real estate adds another layer to his growing portfolio. His properties have included a Kansas City condo and a large Texas home purchased for about $3.37 million. The Texas property, spanning roughly 7,800 square feet, was later estimated to be worth substantially more.There is also a family connection behind Mahomes' sporting success. His father, Pat Mahomes Sr, enjoyed a long Major League Baseball career, appearing in more than 300 games. His professional earnings were modest compared with his son's extraordinary financial rise, but the elder Mahomes gave Patrick an early connection to elite sport.For Mahomes, the bigger story is no longer simply how much he earns as an NFL quarterback. It is how effectively he is converting fame, capital and sporting interests into long-term ownership. If that strategy continues, his playing career could ultimately become just one part of a much larger financial legacy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

While Erica Donald posted on X, "I let him out of the house y’all," the brooding NFL defensive lineman told reporters he had to make sure his wife and household were good with him going back onto the field. I got to make sure that the household was good, the kids were okay with it all," he said. "Then having the hard conversations, figuring things out, what I wanted to do. If I was to do it, how would we do it? "My wife was on board. She said, 'If you want to do this, (I'm) with (you) 100%,' and there were days when I was like, 'I don't know.' She talked to me enough to be like, 'You want to do this. Don't make no decisions faster than what you need to make a decision. Take your time.' She played a huge part of me figuring this out because it really wasn't an easy decision. It took a lot of hard work, a lot of long conversations with a lot of different people, but I felt good enough to make the decision to come back and do this." I knew the world was saying all types of different things and nobody knew what was going on, but I knew for two weeks," Donald said. "Then, I talked to Sean every single week, damn near every day. We stayed in contact. I gave him all my updates, how I was feeling, how things were going. I know he got annoyed with [media] asking all the questions in camp every damn day. I just wanted to take my time and make the right decision because once you choose to come back, you’re all the way back in. You can't be halfway in, you (have to) be all the way in it. I had to get to that point where I felt like I'm 100% committed to playing football again because the last two years have been amazing. Building things that I've been building, working on what I've been working on, working from home, and jumping back in the fire playing football again. So, I really had to sit back, think about it, not just from the physical aspect (but) from the mental aspect as well. Everything just played out how it played out and we're here now." articles.title: Delhi voter roll revision: Here’s what to do if your name is missing from draft list
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The draft electoral roll prepared under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Delhi was published on Monday, leaving out more than 47 lak.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The draft electoral roll prepared under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Delhi was published on Monday, leaving out more than 47 lakh of the 1.45 crore electors on the existing roll.Voters whose names are missing can file claims for inclusion between August 31 and September 30, with the final electoral roll scheduled to be published on November 4.How to check your name in Delhi draft voter listVoters can check whether their names feature in the draft roll through the Delhi chief electoral officer’s website and the Election Commission’s electoral search portal, news agency PTI reported.Search by EPIC: Select Delhi as the state, enter the EPIC number and captcha code, and search for the name.Search by mobile number: Select Delhi and the preferred language, enter the mobile number registered with the Election Commission and the captcha code, then click on Search.Name missing from draft roll? Here’s what to doEligible voters whose names do not appear in the draft roll can seek inclusion during the claims and objections period from August 31 to September 30.Applicants will have to submit Form 6, along with the prescribed Declaration form and supporting documents.Those who have permanently shifted residence and want their names transferred to another constituency can submit Form 6 at their new place of residence.Why are 47.5 lakh names missing?The house-to-house enumeration exercise covered all 1,45,10,299 electors on the existing roll. Completed enumeration forms for more than 67% of electors were submitted and digitised by Booth Level Officers (BLOs).The remaining 47,56,722 electors were categorised as "uncollectable" under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others (ASDDO) category and were consequently not included in the draft roll.Most electors placed in the ASDDO category were marked as "permanently shifted". Their exclusion from the draft does not stop eligible voters from seeking inclusion during the claims period.What is Form 6?Form 6 is the application used to seek inclusion of a name in the electoral roll under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.Applicants need to submit documents establishing their date of birth and residence.For proof of birth, any one of the following can be submitted:Birth certificate issued by the competent local body or Registrar of Births and DeathsAadhaar cardPAN cardDriving licenceClass X or Class XII certificate issued by CBSE, ICSE or a state boardIndian passportIf none of these documents is available, the applicant can provide the required details along with a self-attested copy of an address proof in the name of the applicant or one of their parents, spouse or adult children, as prescribed.Documents accepted as proof of residenceApplicants can submit any one of the following:Water, electricity or gas connection bill for the address for at least one yearAadhaar cardCurrent passbook of a nationalised or scheduled bank or post officeIndian passportRevenue Department land-owning records, including Kisan BahiRegistered rent lease deed, in case of a tenantRegistered sale deed, in case of an ownerHow to submit Form 6A completed Form 6 can be submitted online through the Election Commission’s Voters’ Services Portal (voters.eci.gov.in) or the ECINET app.It can also be submitted offline to the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) or Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), or through the Booth Level Officer (BLO).For most voters, submitting the form online is the simplest option.Why is the SIR being conducted?The Special Intensive Revision is a house-to-house verification exercise aimed at preparing accurate and updated electoral rolls and removing errors and ineligible entries.During the exercise, BLOs visit households to verify voter details and collect updated information.A Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was conducted across the country during 2002-2004.For SIR 2026, the house-to-house enumeration exercise began on June 30 and ended on August 17.The draft roll was published on August 31, marking the start of the claims and objections period, which will continue until September 30.The claims and objections will subsequently be examined, with the notice and disposal process scheduled to conclude on October 29. articles.title: “This is a crime against nature": Travis Kelce sparks outrage with bizarre cereal business venture that leaves fans divided
articles.summary: NFL News: Jason and Travis Kelce once again found a way to turn their brotherly chemistry into a business idea, this time with a bowl and a spoon. In July 2024,.
articles.body: Jason and Travis Kelce once again found a way to turn their brotherly chemistry into a business idea, this time with a bowl and a spoon. In July 2024, the NFL stars announced Kelce Mix, a limited cereal blend that brought together three familiar favourites. The unusual combination quickly became the talking point, with fans divided between curiosity and disbelief over what the brothers had created.Kelce Mix cereal combines three popular breakfast favouritesKelce Mix was built around a simple idea: take three well-known cereals and put them together in one box. The blend brought Cinnamon Toast Crunch, Lucky Charms and Reese’s Puffs into the same mix.On paper, each cereal has its own loyal following. Together, though, the combination created a very different reaction.The announcement spread quickly among fans, many of whom could not decide whether the mixture sounded brilliant or completely wrong. Rather than creating another standard celebrity food product, the Kelce brothers leaned into something playful and familiar.The reaction was immediate.“This is a crime against nature,” one fan said.Another questioned the unlikely career boost surrounding the brothers, while a third summed up the appeal with a joke:“Sounds like diabetes but delicious,” a third fan said.Other reactions showed just how divided the cereal crowd was.“I’m sorry but that blend looks gross!” a fourth fan said.And one fan admitted that the ingredients were already among their personal favourites, but still had doubts about mixing them together:“My top 3 cereals but idk how i feel about them mixed,” a fifth fan said.That uncertainty was part of what made Kelce Mix stand out. The product did not need everyone to agree on the flavour. The unusual pairing itself gave fans something to talk about.Jason and Travis Kelce turn their fame into another ventureThe cereal arrived as another example of the Kelce brothers expanding their work outside the football field.Jason Kelce had retired from the NFL after the 2023 season, but retirement did not mean stepping away from the spotlight. By 2024, he was preparing for his role with ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage while continuing to co-host the New Heights podcast with Travis.Jason described the move to ESPN as an unexpected continuation of his football journey.“Turns out, it was a short retirement!” he joked.“ESPN was a consistent presence in our household growing up and the network helped shape who I am and my love of all sports.“To now appear on that same screen is a full circle moment.“And, I mean it’s freaking Monday Night Football! and I’m ready for some football.”Travis, meanwhile, was still active with the Kansas City Chiefs and had already developed a growing list of business interests. At the time, reports also suggested he was exploring opportunities in the hotel and resort industry.But Kelce Mix offered something different. It was light, accessible and closely tied to the brothers' personalities. Instead of selling a complicated investment story, Jason and Travis put three childhood-style breakfast favourites into one box and let the internet decide whether the result was genius or a “crime against nature.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Allen, New Era Unveil 2026 'Billustration' Hats Designed by 8 Children at Children's Hospital
articles.summary: New Era unveiled eight new hats designed by kids receiving treatment at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo as part of Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's "Billustration" initiative on Monday.
articles.body:
New Era unveiled eight new hats designed by kids receiving treatment at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo as part of Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's "Billustration" initiative on Monday.

All eight hats will be available for purchase on New Era's website, at their stores and at the Bills' merchandise store at Highmark Stadium, and each purchase will benefit the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo.

This marks the second year of the Billustration campaign after $140,230 was raised for the hospital through Billustration in 2025.

Allen released a statement regarding the continuation of the Billustration initiative as part of a press release, saying, "I am incredibly proud of everything last season's Billustration campaign with New Era achieved and I was eager to bring it back for the 2026 season in response to the demand from fans to get their hands on these special caps. Knowing fans can now collect every design and wear them alongside me all season makes it even more special as we continue to support the Patricia Allen Fund and the amazing care provided at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo."

Allen will wear each of the eight hats during the 2026 NFL regular season, as he will don a different one during his tunnel walk prior to each of the Bills' eight home games.

Each hat features Allen's famous drawing of a Bills logo on the front, but they will have differing colors and designs on the side.

The first Billustration hat will be shown off by Allen on Sept. 17 when Buffalo hosts the Detroit Lions in its home opener and the first regular-season game ever played at the new Highmark Stadium.

articles.title: "What a blessing": Russell Wilson and Ciara’s new horse-racing venture gets dream start as Club Reign storms to six-length win
articles.summary: NFL News: Russell Wilson and Ciara have found a new arena for competition, and their first outing could hardly have gone better. The couple’s Three Brand Racing.
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara have found a new arena for competition, and their first outing could hardly have gone better. The couple’s Three Brand Racing made its debut at Saratoga on Travers Day, with Club Reign delivering a six-length victory in the opening race. For Wilson, the former NFL star now preparing for his television career, the win offered an unexpected but familiar feeling: the thrill of coming out on top.Russell Wilson and Ciara celebrate winning debut with Three Brand RacingClub Reign wasted little time making an impression. The two-year-old powered away from six other horses to claim victory at Saratoga Race Course, giving Wilson and Ciara an ideal introduction to thoroughbred ownership.The result was especially meaningful because this was not simply another investment for the couple. Wilson has described Three Brand Racing as a family-focused project, making the first victory a moment they could enjoy together.“Man, what an exciting day,” Wilson said afterward. “We’re so excited for Three Brand Racing and, obviously, Club Reign. What a blessing.”Wilson already had plenty of confidence in Club Reign before the race. The performance, however, gave that belief some serious backing. The horse was ridden by Edgard Zayas and trained by Whit Beckman, with the combination producing a commanding result on one of the biggest days on the Saratoga calendar.“We felt like we had a tremendous athlete in this horse,” Wilson said. “He’s our first one for me and Ciara and our team, our Three Brand Racing team, and to come out here and to win in Saratoga—and he won by a lot. He’s a fast horse.”Ciara and the couple’s children were also present for the winner’s-circle celebration. That family element matters to Wilson, who sees horse racing as more than a new business interest.Russell Wilson brings his competitive spirit to horse racingWilson's interest in horse racing did not appear out of nowhere. He credited his brother Harry, who lives in Louisville, Kentucky, with helping introduce him to the world of thoroughbred ownership. Their daughter Sienna, meanwhile, already enjoys horseback riding, giving the family another personal connection to the sport.“We felt like this would be a good thing for the family,” Wilson explained. “No matter what happens, let’s do some cool stuff. I love competing, I love our family competing, and our Three Brand Racing team loves it, too.”That competitive edge has been a major part of Wilson's life for years. After 14 NFL seasons, he retired with 46,966 passing yards, 353 touchdowns and a Super Bowl XLVIII title with the Seattle Seahawks.His next chapter will take him to CBS Sports, where he is set to work as an analyst. But horse racing has already given him another way to experience the rush of competition.“There’s nothing like holding that Lombardi Trophy in front of hundreds and hundreds of millions of people,” Wilson said.Even so, winning immediately at Saratoga clearly made an impression.“To win on Travers Day, to win in Saratoga first race out, it feels like rookie of the year.”Then came a familiar phrase from Zayas after the victory.“He comes right up to me and goes, ‘Let’s ride,’” Wilson recalled.Wilson could only laugh. “So, that was funny.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why is Shilo Sanders facing an $11.89 million bankruptcy trial as Deion Sanders' son fights to erase massive debt?
articles.summary: NFL News: Shilo Sanders, the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers' star player, has found himself in a difficult spot as his federal bankruptcy trial is all set to begin.
articles.body: Shilo Sanders, the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers' star player, has found himself in a difficult spot as his federal bankruptcy trial is all set to begin today, months after he stopped training and effectively retired from the league. The focus remains on whether his $11.89 million debt could be erased.Why is Shilo Sanders being put on trial and sued by a security guard?More than a decade ago, in 2015, Deion Sanders’ son, Shilo Sanders, got involved in an altercation with a security guard named John Darjean, when he was still a high school student.John Darjean has accused Shiloh Sanders that he was physically assaulted by the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers' player and was permanently injured. The altercation happened as he tried to confiscate Shilo Sanders’ phone since his father, Deion Sanders, requested for it.Interestingly, this is not the first time that the case has actually gone to trial. Back in 2022, Shilo Sanders had skipped the trial and John Darjean sued and won an $11.89 million default judgment.A few months later, in October 2023, Shilo Sanders filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in October 2023 to eliminate this massive debt, but the drama did not end there.John Darjean argued in court that the massive $11.89 million debt cannot be erased because it came from a "willful and malicious injury".According to reports, a pretrial statement filed by the parties in the case, states that Shilo Sanders “contends that his actions were justified in that any force used by (Sanders) was reasonable and immediately necessary to protect himself against (Darjean’s) own use or attempted use of improper force.”While Shilo Sanders’ legal team has stated that Deion Sanders will not be required to testify, the judge has asked him to be available on 4th September.Has Shilo Sanders retired from the NFL after an effectively short lived career on the field?As Shilo Sanders remains busy fighting in court, many are concerned about his career.A few months ago, on his YouTube as fans asked whether he has retired, Shilo Sanders said, "You don't give up on playing in the NFL, bro. If they don't call me to get on the team, I cannot play. What do you want me to do? Force them to say, 'Hey, bro, sign me.' It don't work like that. Y'all quit asking me that stupid question. This is stupid. It don't work like that. Y'all think the NFL is like high school football?"He added, "I just be like working out like just as a human. But training and stuff, like getting ready, and you have a set day, like camp starts, like a whole different type of training. It takes a special kind of guy to see the light at the end of the tunnel, and I don't think there's any light in my tunnel."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
