articles.body: Travis Kelce is getting a crash course in family life - and his big brother Jason Kelce’s parenting advice is anything but usual.Just two months after his wedding to a billionaire pop singer, Travis found himself at the nucleus of a befitting New Heights throwback involving parenting, kids, and one utterly wild claim about cats.The official New Heights X account recently resurrected one of the podcast’s most unforgettable moments while counting down the Top 92 moments in New Heights history.And Jason’s honest confession immediately eclipsed everything else.The former Philadelphia Eagles center revealed that he once told his children cats were poisonous because he didn’t want his family to get one.Yes, Jason Kelce apparently decided that petrifying his girls with a feline-related warning was easier than simply saying no.Jason Kelce’s parenting confession to Travis Kelce is peak Kelce momentIf there is one thing fans have learned from New Heights, it is that the Kelce brothers have no shortage of scandalously shocking family stories.Jason’s cat confession might be one of the funniest to date [you can agree to disagree].Rather than negotiating with his daughters over getting a pet, the retired NFL star apparently went straight for the ultimate hindrance: convincing them that cats were dangerous.And it worked! At least temporarily.But years later, the confession has become another classic New Heights moment, giving fans a glimpse into the surprisingly chaotic parenting style inside the Kelce household. Just that, this time it coincides with Travis’ wedding timeline!Travis Kelce enters a new chapterTravis’ connection to the parenting conversation comes at an interesting point in his life [consider it X timeline, more than actual actual timeline].The Kansas City Chiefs star recently entered married life, adding another major milestone to a career already packed with NFL success, celebrity attention, and record-breaking moments.While the brothers have always discussed their personal lives on New Heights, Jason’s experience as a father gives him a unique perspective when family and parenting enter the conversation.Jason and Kylie Kelce are wonderful parents to four beautiful daughters, so the former NFL star has had innumerable opportunities to learn what works, and, apparently, what certainly should not be repeated.For Travis, his older, sagacious brother could be the zenith source of valuable advice.Or perhaps the supreme source of shocking stories about what not to do.Cyberspace cannot get over the cat storyThe funniest part of the resurfaced moment may be how casually Jason admits to the bizarre strategy.There is no elaborate, exhaustive explanation. No complicated parenting philosophy.Just: cats are poisonous.The confession has all the ingredients of a classic Kelce story: family chaos, sibling banter, and a parenting decision that sounds progressively ridiculous the more you think about it.It also perfectly captures the unique chemistry that has made New Heights such a hit podcast.Travis and Jason may be two of the best-known brothers in sports, but moments like this remind fans that behind the NFL fame are two siblings who still enjoy embarrassing each other and digging up beyond-funny family memories. Because laughter is precious! And it’s best shared with siblings.From football legends to family conversationsThe Kelce brothers built their public personas on football, but New Heights has turned their family dynamic into engrossing entertainment on its own.And with Travis now voyaging a new mountain of life, fans are naturally paying even closer attention whenever the brothers talk about relationships, marriage, family, or parenting.Still, this latest viral moment is less [almost negligible] about Travis reportedly making any major personal announcement and more about Jason proving once again that his parenting stories can be out-and-out unbelievable to ears.After all, several parents have told their children not to touch something. If they did, something would happen.But Jason Kelce apparently decided to make sure his kids stayed away from cats forever.Poisonous cats. Four daughters. Two Kelce brothers. Another unforgettable New Heights moment.And somehow, that sounds exactly like the Kelce family. articles.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft Monday: Final picks for the Vikings before Week 1
articles.summary: In the final preseason mock draft for the Vikings, we give their defense more pieces.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL Draft will take place in Washington, D.C. next year. In that draft, the Vikings still have their first-round pick, but a lot could happen in the next 9 months. Before then, though, there will be plenty of speculation and buildup for the team and who they may add to the roster through the draft in a class that many are saying could be one of generational wealth.

While we will always look at mock drafts from analysts around the space, we will also keep up with our Mock Draft Mondays here on Vikings Wire.

While this used to be just an exercise used for the Fall to introduce players, the 2027 NFL Draft class is too good to be contained to those select months. So with that in mind, let's dive into a 3-Round 2027 NFL Mock Draft for the Vikings.

Round 1: Kelley Jones, CB, Mississippi State

Projected Trade: Vikings send the 15th pick to the San Francisco 49ers for the 23rd and 55th overall picks.

Kelley Jones has positional versatility to play both safety and cornerback, but he is projecting as the latter in the NFL. Jones is someone who could be a reliable piece, and a productive one, in Brian Flores' defense. He likes aggressive and physical defenders, and Jones checks both boxes.

The team has Dallas Turner in place, and perhaps even Jake Golday, to replace Andrew Van Ginkel, who is playing on an expiring contract in 2026. Will Heldt was the best Clemson defender in 2025 and is a very well-rounded edge rusher. He can defend the run and has some decent pass-rushing chops to boot. Adding him to the pass rush rotation would be a good idea for the team.

The Vikings have clearly made it a point to have depth at the wide receiver position as they are three deep in 2026. Jauan Jennings is on a one-year deal, and if they want to replace him, Wingo would be a good option. He can take the top off of defenses, be physical blocking, and fit into what they look for in a receiver.

Bray Hubbard is a rangy safety for the Crimson Tide defense who also boasts good instincts. He tracks the ball well, provides run support, and is someone who could be a part of the safety trio the Vikings like to boast. He is no Harrison Smith, but he can find the ball enough that he can help force turnovers the way Smith did.

articles.title: 3 Colts roster cuts who could be claimed on waivers by another team
articles.summary: These three former Colts who were released during roster cutdowns could be claimed on waivers by another team.
articles.body:
A few players who were cut by the Indianapolis Colts could draw interest from other NFL teams.

Next up in the roster-building process for NFL teams is scouring the waiver wire market for players to add to their respective 53-man rosters.

Players who have fewer than four accrued NFL seasons are subject to waivers. If a team wants to add one of those players to their team, they will put in a claim. If multiple teams put in a claim, then that player goes to the team with the higher priority, which at this time of the year is determined by the original 2026 draft order before trades.

As teams look to continue tweaking their final rosters, here are a few now-former Colts players who could end up playing elsewhere this season.

The Colts' decision to release Wooden was a surprise. He brings a versatile skill set to a defensive front -- able to play across multiple gaps -- and Wooden can also impact both the run and pass games.

Grupe had his ups and downs in the preseason, but he was overall steady this summer, including training camp practices, and was perfect during the second half of last year. A team with uncertainty at kicker could look to bring Grupe in.

Bentley had a good showing this summer, to the point where he very much could have earned a roster spot with the Colts. For a team that is looking to add a pass-catching presence out of the backfield, Bentley could be a valuable addition.

Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, Derrick Nnadi, and Juanyeh Thomas all have four-plus years of accrued NFL experience, so they are not subject to waivers. As free agents, they are able to sign where they please.

articles.title: Joe Fagnano makes Baltimore Ravens 53-man roster
articles.summary: The best UConn QB since Dan Orlovsky made an NFL roster as an undrafted free agent.
articles.body:
After an unlikely college football journey that ended as a standout at UConn, and then joining the NFL as an undrafted rookie, Joe Fagnano is on the roster for the Baltimore Ravens.

Fagnano began his college career in 2019 as a walk-on at FCS Maine. He quickly earned a scholarship and then playing time after the incumbent starter was injured, starting games against Richmond and Liberty, among others.

In 2023, Fagnano followed Nick Charlton to UConn. Charlton was the Maine head coach and became the OC for Jim Mora's Huskies and Fagnano transferred to earn a starting role. He was up against high level recruits or big NIL additions throughout his time as a Husky, but he persevered and ended up setting the program's passing records in 2025.

In his final year as a Husky, Fagnano completed 69 percent of his passes for 28 touchdowns with just one interception the whole season. He earned an NFL Combine invite for his efforts but went undrafted, choosing to sign with the Ravens though he was not actively recruited as a UDFA. He was a mini-camp invitee.

Diego Pavia, the Heisman semifinalist from Vanderbilt, was also in camp but was cut in the summer. Fagnano signed through the preseason and then wowed in three opportunities on the field, leading the NFL in passing yards over the three week exhibition period. The Ravens had the option to waive him and try to stash him on the practice squad, but after that preseason performance, it seemed likely that another team would try to pick him up. They've rostered him because they're clearly excited for his potential, even though he's a 25-year-old rookie.

Elsewhere around the league, fourth-round pick Skyler Bell is on the Bills' roster after a late, great preseason debut. DT Travis Jones is still thriving on the Ravens. OTs Matthew Peart and Ryan Van Demark are entering their 7th and 5th NFL seasons, respectively, and DT Foley Fatukasi signed with the Las Vegas Raiders this offseason for his 8th season.

Former Huskies Chase Lundt, Louis Hansen, Justin Joly, Cam Ross, Zavier Scott, Nate Carter, Keelan Marion, Nathan Voorhis, and Valentin Senn were cut on the final day, but should have a strong shot at making a practice squad.
